claims.claim: With external anchors and a pinned key, a rewrite, rollback, deletion or fork of the events an anchor covers fails verification, re-hashed or not.

statements.text: Even a fully re-hashed, internally-consistent rewrite of the events an anchor covers fails verification against the externally-held root; events appended after the last anchor are covered only by the next one.

With [external anchoring](https://github.com/usertools-ai/usertrust/blob/master/docs/anchoring.md) enabled, verification goes further: the auditor fetches signed checkpoints from an append-only store the operator cannot rewrite and pins the public key out-of-band — so even a fully re-hashed rewrite of the events an anchor covers fails:
Competing records at the same position in the append-only store are cryptographic fork evidence.
| `ANCHOR_MISMATCH` | valid signature, content contradicts the vault: rewrite, rollback, deletion, fork | **1** |
| Roll back to an older, internally-valid snapshot | `ANCHOR_MISMATCH` — anchored size exceeds observed size |

Even a fully re-hashed, internally-consistent rewrite of the events an anchor covers fails verification against the externally-held root; events appended after the last anchor are covered only by the next one.

With [external anchoring](https://github.com/usertools-ai/usertrust/blob/master/docs/anchoring.md) enabled, verification goes further: the auditor fetches signed checkpoints from an append-only store the operator cannot rewrite and pins the public key out-of-band — so even a fully re-hashed rewrite of the events an anchor covers fails:

This upgrades the guarantee from *tamper-evident if you trust the operator's files* to **independently verifiable**: even a fully re-hashed, internally-consistent rewrite fails against the externally-held root.

Result states: `ANCHORED_VERIFIED`, `UNANCHORED` (legacy vaults — valid, weaker, labeled), `ANCHOR_UNVERIFIABLE`, `ANCHOR_STALE`, and the hard failures `ANCHOR_INVALID` / `ANCHOR_MISMATCH` (rewrite, rollback, deletion, or fork against the signed checkpoints — always exit 1).

claims.claim: The anchor store's append-only property comes from the store's own configuration (Object Lock, ownership, WORM), not from usertrust.

statements.text: **External anchoring** — Ed25519-signed chain-head checkpoints pushed to an append-only store the vault operator cannot rewrite (S3 Object Lock, protected git branch, SIEM).

External anchoring closes that gap: the writer periodically emits a **signed checkpoint** of the chain head (Merkle root + size + last hash, Ed25519-signed, hash-chained to the previous checkpoint) to an **append-only store the vault operator cannot silently rewrite**.
Immutable object names mean an overwrite attempt of a past anchor is a denied write, never a silent replace — and a bucket listing exposes the true anchor high-water mark in one command.
**SIEM (Splunk HEC / Datadog logs)** — `--sink-url https://…` POSTs each record; SIEM ingest credentials are inherently append-only.
WORM guarantees come from the store's own configuration — S3 Object Lock compliance-mode retention, POSIX ownership, an appliance's WORM mode.
- **Compromise**: a stolen key can sign forks — it cannot rewrite stored anchors.
The append-only witness, not the key custody, is the control for that.
**External anchoring** — Ed25519-signed chain-head checkpoints pushed to an append-only store the vault operator cannot rewrite (S3 Object Lock, protected git branch, SIEM).
- **External anchors** (optional) — binds the vault to Ed25519-signed checkpoints held in an append-only store the vault operator cannot rewrite.

claims.claim: anchor doctor probes permissions; it is not proof that the store is append-only.

statements.text: Doctor is a **permission probe, not proof of immutability**.
| `--sink-file` | creates `.doctor-probe-<pid>` in the store's directory, then attempts `unlink` (`delete-denied`) and in-place truncation (`overwrite-denied`).
| `--sink-url`, `--sink-rekor`, `command` | `info` — no probe is possible from here; verify the append-only property at the receiving system. |
- **POSIX directory semantics.** Deletion is governed by write permission on the *directory*; in-place truncation is governed by permission on the *file*.

claims.claim: A Rekor receipt is verified offline: checkpoint signature, inclusion path, and binding to the anchor record; a SET is what attests integratedTime.

statements.text: What ships now is the complete, tested verification path — receipt schema, > signed-note checkpoints, RFC 9162 inclusion, SET-verified attested time — plus a sink that works > against any log accepting these entries.

Verification is offline and zero-dependency: the signed-note checkpoint is parsed and its ECDSA P-256 signature checked, inclusion is proven by an RFC 9162 index-based path walk, and the stored entry is bound to *your* record by payload hash and by decoded signature bytes.
Receipts *without* a SET still prove inclusion, but fall back to operator-claimed time for freshness: an unsigned `integratedTime` is a number the party under audit could have chosen.

**Checkpoint-replay caveat.** Offline verification proves the entry was included in the log — *at `integratedTime`* only when a SET vouches for that time — under a checkpoint signed by the pinned key.
A verified receipt also makes `--max-anchor-age` measure against the log's attested `integratedTime` instead of the operator's own timestamp.

claims.claim: Every governed call is recorded on the audit chain, or its receipt carries auditDegraded and verify reports the missing event.

statements.text: Every governed LLM call becomes a tamper-evident, auditable transaction.

Every governed call is metered, policy-checked and recorded on the audit chain; a call whose record could not be written says so on its receipt (`auditDegraded`, see [LIMITATIONS.md, section 5](https://github.com/usertools-ai/usertrust/blob/master/LIMITATIONS.md#5-one-audit-writer-per-vault-one-process-at-a-time)).

Every governed call is metered, policy-checked and recorded on the audit chain; a call whose record could not be written says so on its receipt (`auditDegraded`, see [LIMITATIONS.md, section 5](https://github.com/usertools-ai/usertrust/blob/master/LIMITATIONS.md#5-one-audit-writer-per-vault-one-process-at-a-time)).
The call is recorded on the tamper-evident audit chain; if that write fails, a `USERTRUST_AUDIT_DEGRADED` warning reports it and the event is dead-lettered.
Every governed LLM call produces an audit event; a call whose event could not be written says so on its receipt (see [Dead-Letter Queue](#dead-letter-queue)).

Every governed local call still places a PENDING hold, settles at least 1 usertoken, and is recorded on the audit chain (or, if that write fails, its receipt carries `auditDegraded`) -- so runaway loops burn budget, anomaly governance still fires, and every governed call has a receipt.

usertrust wraps any LLM client (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google) with a JS Proxy so every governed AI call becomes an auditable, double-entry financial transaction, recorded on a tamper-evident audit chain.
Every governed call appends a SHA-256-hashed event to `.usertrust/audit/events.jsonl` (a call whose event could not be written says so on its receipt, as `auditDegraded`).

denied.why: A call that does not fit its budget is refused before egress (budget-refused-before-egress), but a call's real cost can exceed its hold: content passed by reference, tool declarations resolved after authorization, an uncapped output above 4096 tokens, and an estimate not calibrated to any tokenizer. The excess is recorded as a settlement_shortfall event, not prevented, and dryRun and allowUngoverned calls hold nothing. So no agent STARTS a call its budget cannot cover; it can still spend past what its hold reserved.

contradictedBy.text: A call whose real cost turns out above its hold is posted capped at the hold, and the truncation is recorded as a `settlement_shortfall` event: visible, never silent.
